ProtT5 DNA Binding Prediction — Interpretation Report

Source: ProtT5_DNA_binding_clean_pipeline.ipynb  |  Model: ProtT5 • 1024-dim  |  Task: Binary classification (DNA-binding vs Non-DNA-binding)

1. Dataset

UniProtKB Swiss-Prot reviewed proteins split by the DNA binding annotation column:

  • Positive (DNA-binding): proteins with at least one annotated DNA_BIND feature
  • Negative (non-DNA-binding): proteins with no DNA binding annotation
  • Mutual exclusivity enforced — no protein appears in both sets
  • Duplicate protein names removed (keep first)
Class Imbalance Warning: The dataset is highly imbalanced (~1:31 ratio). All classifiers use imbalance correction (LR: class_weight="balanced"; MLP: BCEWithLogitsLoss(pos_weight)). PR-AUC is a more informative metric than ROC-AUC under severe imbalance.

2. Methods

2.1 Full-protein Pooled Embeddings

ProtT5 (Elnaggar et al., 2022) produces 1024-dimensional per-residue representations, aggregated to fixed-length protein vectors via:

  • Max pooling — element-wise maximum over residues
  • Attention pooling — learned weighted average over residues

All features z-score normalised (StandardScaler fit on train only). 80/20 stratified split, seed 42.

2.2 DNA-binding Domain 21-mer Window Embeddings

Per-residue ProtT5 embeddings (.pt files, plain torch.Tensor of shape L×1024) are loaded for each protein. A 21-residue window is centred on the midpoint of the first annotated UniProt DNA_BIND domain range and mean-pooled to a 1024-dim vector. Additionally, 3 random non-domain windows from the same protein (positive label) are included, and equal-count random windows from non-DNA-binding proteins (negative label) are added.

ParameterValue
Window size21 residues (10 on each side of domain midpoint)
PoolingMean over window residues → 1024-dim vector
Non-domain windows per protein3
Negative windowsRandom windows from non-DNA-binding proteins
ClassifierMLP: 1024→512→256→1 (binary), 30 epochs, Adam lr=1e-3

2.3 Classifiers (full-protein)

ModelArchitectureImbalance handling
Logistic RegressionL2 penalty, lbfgs, max_iter=5000class_weight="balanced"
MLP (PyTorch) Linear(1024→512)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→ Linear(512→256)→ReLU→Dropout(0.3)→Linear(256→1), Adam lr=1e-3, 30 epochs, batch=64, BCEWithLogitsLoss pos_weight = n_neg / n_pos

4. DNA-binding Domain 21-mer Window Analysis

This analysis tests whether a 21-residue window centred on the annotated DNA-binding domain (as defined by UniProt DNA_BIND feature) carries sufficient discriminative signal to distinguish DNA-binding from non-DNA-binding regions using only local sequence context. Windows are mean-pooled from per-residue ProtT5 embeddings (L×1024 plain tensors).

Interpretation: Comparing the domain window ROC-AUC (0.9780) to the full-protein best (0.9771) shows the 21-mer domain window captures a comparable or stronger signal to full-protein embeddings. A high domain window score indicates the ProtT5 model encodes distinct local chemistry around DNA-binding domains.

6. Recommendations for Future Work

  1. Cross-validation: Use 5-fold stratified CV to reduce variance from single splits.
  2. Better negatives: Use structurally similar non-binding proteins as hard negatives.
  3. All domains: Use all annotated DNA_BIND ranges per protein, not just the first.
  4. Window sweep: Compare window sizes 11, 21, 41, 61 for optimal context.
  5. Fine-tuning: End-to-end fine-tune ProtT5 for DNA-binding prediction.
